scenario.name: Freedesktop Systemd Spec & Elastic DFIR — Linux systemd Generator (/run/systemd/generator) & Unit Persistence Forensics
scenario.overview: Picture a bustling restaurant kitchen with a stainless-steel pass-through counter, a hanging rail of paper order tickets, a glowing drive-thru window, and a line chef at the stove. Pulling up to the restaurant drive-thru window, a clever customer asks for a routine meal while sneaking an extra kitchen command onto the special-notes line of the order. In this real-world scenario, the intruder approaches the drive-thru order window disguised as a regular visitor, then bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the kitchen order ticket rail. The restaurant manager inspects the kitchen receipt printer tape and spots an impossible order note that gave away stock without a matching sale. In this scenario (T1543.002, Freedesktop Systemd Spec & Elastic DFIR, Linux systemd Generator (/run/systemd/generator) & Unit Persistence Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: dropping Executable Generator, then ephemeral Unit Synthesis, then forensic Attribution via systemctl. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Dropping Executable Generator, then Ephemeral Unit Synthesis, then Forensic Attribution via systemctl, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on auditd Event 257 correlated across the documented kill chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Dropping Executable Generator into /etc/systemd/system-generators/ (auditd PATH Record)
stages.subtitle: Persistence (T1543.002 - Create or Modify System Process: Systemd Service)
stages.description: Pulling up to the restaurant drive-thru window, a clever customer asks for a routine meal while sneaking an extra kitchen command onto the special-notes line of the order. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder approaches the drive-thru order window disguised as a regular visitor while everyday visitors and the line chef go about their routine. Instead of creating a conspicuous unit file directly in /etc/systemd/system/, the actor drops a small executable script at /etc/systemd/system-generators/dbus- early-check (or /usr/lib/systemd/system-generators/). stages.title: Stage 2: Ephemeral Unit Synthesis in /run/systemd/generator/ on systemctl daemon-reload
stages.subtitle: Persistence (T1543.002 - Ephemeral /run/systemd/generator/ Unit Synthesis)
stages.description: When the cashier clips that paper slip onto the stainless-steel kitchen ticket rail, the busy line chef reads the hidden note literally as a direct manager instruction. Here in Step 2 inside the restaurant kitchen, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the kitchen order ticket rail without disturbing the sealed pantry cold room. When systemctl daemon-reload is triggered, systemd (PID 1) invokes /etc/systemd/system-generators/dbus-early-check, passing /run/systemd/generator as argv[1]. stages.title: Stage 3: Forensic Attribution via systemctl statusFragmentPath, systemd-analyze & journalctl _SYSTEMD_UNIT
stages.subtitle: Execution (T1543.002 - FragmentPath & journalctl Forensic Attribution)
stages.description: Instead of serving only the paid sandwich, the kitchen passes the back-office recipe binder and extra stock straight out through the pickup window. In this final step inside the restaurant kitchen, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the kitchen order ticket rail until the kitchen pos receipt printer catches the mismatch. During incident response, running systemctl show -p FragmentPath,SourcePath,ExecStart network-health.service and systemd-analyze unit-paths exposes that the active service originates from /run/systemd/generator/network-health.service, while journalctl _PID=1 correlates the reload timestamp with the generator script (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with UnitName=network-health.service, FragmentPath=/run/systemd/generator/network-health.service , tmpfs, ExecStartBinary=/usr/local/bin/net-telemetry-sync, GeneratorOrigin=/etc/systemd/system-generators/dbus-early-check so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Next, the follow-up artifact systemd-analyze verify /run/systemd/generator/network-health.service runs (which invokes or targets the host daemon/process , systemd-analyze verify /run/systemd/generator/network-health.service with its runtime command-line arg so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1543.002 during "Forensic Attribution via systemctl statusFragmentPath, systemd-analyze & journalctl _SYSTEMD_UNIT" , During incident response, running systemctl show -p FragmentPath,SourcePath,ExecStart network-health while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution).
